items.quote: Arthur's Seat is an ancient extinct volcano. It is the main peak of a group of hills in Edinburgh, Scotland, which form most of Holyrood Park
The Fringe is an open access festival
items.note: Accept "Edinburgh Festival Fringe" too. "Open-access" is what separates it from the Edinburgh International Festival, which also runs in August.

items.quote: was a Skye Terrier or Dandie Dinmont Terrier who became known in 19th-century Edinburgh
items.note: The breed is genuinely disputed (a 2022 book argues Dandie Dinmont Terrier); the question's "traditionally said to be" is what makes Skye Terrier the single answer. Keep that wording.

items.quote: Born and educated in Edinburgh, Stevenson suffered from serious bronchial trouble for much of his life
The Royal Mile runs between Edinburgh Castle and Holyrood Palace
items.note: Wikipedia calls it a "term" for a series of streets rather than a nickname; harmless.

items.quote: The collective name "Waverley", after the Waverley Novels by Sir Walter Scott
He is best known for his four novels and fifty-six short stories about the fictional consulting detective Sherlock Holmes
Edinburgh lies on the southern shore of the Firth of Forth
The One O'Clock Gun is a time signal, fired every day at precisely one p.m., excepting Sunday, Good Friday and Christmas Day
The city is nicknamed Auld Reekie, Scots for Old Smoky, for the views from the country of the smoke-covered Old Town
items.note: Accept "smoke" / "smell"? Only smoke is supported; "smell" is a common pub guess and should be marked wrong.
